supersedes.reason: After the prior remediation was approved and fast-forwarded to local main, the required main/branch checkout cycle materialized governed text fixtures with Windows CRLF bytes. Raw fixture hashing then rejected an otherwise identical clean checkout. This correction canonicalizes only governed UTF-8 text line endings, rejects bare carriage returns, and preserves content-drift denial.

checks.result: At exact clean post-checkout commit 9f94e94, the desktop and 10,000-row component measurements pass with canonical fixture hashes equal to the reviewed baseline: cold p95 36 ms, visible p95 17.215 ms, usable p95 19.092 ms, and component p95 41.193 ms below the 46.916 ms relative and 100 ms absolute limits. Report SHA-256: 8ea4aa01a1cace797aed4fde2dafc242b3223af9a0386831dca161482a932295.

All 12 focused tests pass. The new regression proves LF and CRLF checkouts produce the same canonical fixture SHA-256, actual content drift changes the digest, and a bare carriage return fails closed; all prior strict baseline, sample, URL, budget, and methodology attacks remain denied.
The complete active T03 range retains exactly the approved seven governed UI files and unchanged reference identity; this verifier-only portability fix introduces no application or reference content.
All 57 governed Python files, the active campaign ledger, and generated planning views pass.

evidence: The independently approved recovery behavior and bounded interactive DataTable are unchanged; the exact post-checkout benchmark now remains available on the release-authoritative Windows platform.
Only UTF-8 CRLF-to-LF canonicalization is permitted for governed text fixture identity. Content changes remain hash-visible, invalid UTF-8 fails decoding, and bare carriage returns are rejected.
No product, UI reference, component, route, service, storage, or native behavior changed.
The 12 focused tests include the clean Windows line-ending regression and retain every strict baseline and sample denial test.
The exact clean performance report replays all 20 component batches and passes both regression limits after the real main/branch checkout sequence that exposed the defect.
The previously approved real-browser 10,000-row interaction harness remains byte-identical and applicable.
The six-file incremental range contains only immutable prior evidence, its task-state transitions, the existing desktop performance verifier, and its focused regression tests.
No verification-profile or protected UI-gate control changed; the active UI gate, quality checks, ledger, and generated views all pass.
The canonical digest values remain the reviewed LF source hashes, so the correction does not silently rebaseline fixture content.

reviewerDisposition.note: Independent review must reproduce clean LF/CRLF equivalence, content-drift and bare-CR denial, exact six-file scope, unchanged canonical fixture hashes, clean performance, and the unchanged approved interaction/product boundaries.
